headline: The docs have the right shape: two tracks, no broken links, an honest install guide. What is missing is a working path from "installed" to "first result", symptom-worded help that search can find, and a handful of wrong UI labels. All of that is mostly small edits in the template repo plus 4 small site changes, not new machinery.

implement_now.title: Fix wrong or stale UI labels and typos in the template guides
implement_now.what: One small PR in CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor, .tools/docs only, each label re-checked against the code at edit time (the local checkouts are on stale branches; read origin/main). (1) notebook_upload.md:143: 'Click **Validate submission**' becomes 'Click **Validate & Add Submission**' (form app.py:1029); one sentence that the notebook then appears in the 'Submission list' and several notebooks can be added before 'Upload it to GitHub' / 'Create pull request'; use the real label '🚀 Create pull request' in step 6. (2) notebook_usage.md: 'Ctrl + C or Cmd + C' becomes 'press Ctrl+C in the terminal window' (on macOS Cmd+C copies; Ctrl+C is the interrupt); 'Open the Notebook' becomes 'Open the notebook' (Welcome_template.ipynb); fix 'finnisehd' and 'LabConstrisctor'. (3) workflow_status.md lines 17-20: the log artifact is a plain .log file ('archive: false' in release_constructor.yml and update_on_notebook_change.yml), so replace 'usually a .zip, unzip it' with 'download the log file'. (4) personal_access_token.md: remove the 'repo > contents' sub-bullets and the invented classic-token 'Resource owner' step; tell the reader to tick 'repo'; add 'The repository form accepts only a classic token (it starts with ghp_)'; drop or honestly rename the 'Read-Only Access' recipe (a classic repo-scope token is read+write). (5) initialise_repository.md: use 0.0.1 as the example version (form app.py:870 and release guide), and say the section is titled 'Initialise GitHub repository' (app.py:838), not 'Initialise a repository'. (6) accept_pull_request.md: 'Got to' becomes 'Go to'. (7) before_getting_started.md line 27 and executable_creation.md line 21: repair the garbled sentences. (8) template_synchronization.md: 'the following video' becomes 'the GIFs', and change its footer to the standard '[← Previous] | [🏠 Home] | [Next →]' form so the site strips it (today it prints as literal Markdown on /guides/template-synchronization/). (9) .tools/templates/Welcome_template.ipynb line 21: 'Test Connection' becomes 'Load Private GitHub Repo'. Do not touch the GitHub release-form wording or the screenshots until someone has looked at GitHub's current UI.
implement_now.why: Benchmark s6 (UI accuracy) and s1 ('exactly what do I click'). Every item was checked against the source by the auditor and the skeptic (app.py lines, workflow YAML, Welcome template, built site/guides/template-synchronization/index.html:309-311, guides.py:23 NAV_BLOCK needs the words Previous/Next/Home). Wrong labels in a first-time guide are a stop point for a novice, and they are free to fix.

(c) Add one 'Check that it worked' paragraph before '## Next': a terminal window opens, then your browser opens JupyterLab with the Welcome notebook (can take a little while the first time; wording taken from notebook_usage.md section 2), with a link to Troubleshooting an installed app. (d) Add the literal words 'SmartScreen' and 'unidentified developer' next to the existing Windows/macOS step text ONLY if a maintainer confirms that Windows/macOS actually display them. troubleshooting_installed_app.md: (e) fix line 7: the 'uninstalling guide' link goes to download_executable.md, which on the template is the 'Sorry, but no executable files are available yet' stub; do NOT repoint to install.md (the same file is copied into every app repo where install.md does not exist and where download_executable.md has real per-app text, e.g. NucleiSky/.tools/docs/download_executable.md:188). guide_convention: Lightweight convention for the five critical how-to guides only (install, initialise-repository, notebook-requirements, notebook-upload, executable-creation) and the /submit/ page; explanation and reference pages and the three plugin guides are not required to follow it. Three H2 headings, written in the owning repo (template .tools/docs for the first five, content/submit.md for submit): 'What you need' (or 'Before you start'), 'Check that it worked', 'If something does not work' (the plugin guides' existing wording). No new required 'Next' or time heading: install already has a measured time, and 'Next' is handled by the pager and by hand-written sections where the target exists. Every guide still has an outcome-bearing opening paragraph (already enforced by guides.describe). Time or expected output are stated only when measured or observed. Enforcement: data/guides.yaml gets a `critical:` slug list (author-controlled, in the site repo); a new scripts/lcsite/guide_shape.py with a pure missing_sections(markdown, wanted) is called from scripts/check_site.py, not from the build, and reports 'WARNING <guide>: missing section <heading>' into build/problems.md, like warn_unlisted. Failure becomes fail() naming the file and heading only after the template pages comply, so another repo's edit cannot stop the Pages deploy while the guides are still being brought up to the standard. Tests: tests/test_guide_shape.py covers a pass case, a missing-section case and an unknown slug (raises). DESIGN.md documents the three headings first. A second small check in check_site.py fails on literal Markdown '](' in rendered text.

If app owners actually use quickstart/docs_url, add one optional manifest object `example` ({guide_url, data_url, tested_with}) with a 'Try an example' section; schema authority is the site repo and must be copied to LabConstrictor .tools/schema and .template_sync/resources and LabConstrictor_streamlit schemas/, with DESIGN.md first and tests.

A banner in LabConstrictor/.tools/docs/README.md that copies in app repos may be out of date, with the current guide link on the site (all 6 app repos carry stale .tools/docs; template_version 0.1.3 to 0.1.14 versus 0.1.15 on main).

One help line in the Welcome notebook (template Welcome_template.ipynb has no mention of help, issues or documentation) pointing at the App Centre page's Report a problem; propagates through template sync.

Stable address policy for links shipped inside software (the Welcome notebook hard-codes a template blob/main personal_access_token.md URL; the form hard-codes 9 template doc URLs): record in the template README that doc renames need a migration note.

Optional per-repo CODEOWNERS and per-release docs review checklist (docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md) listing the critical walkthroughs, with the date, person and versions of the last run; and a pre-merge contract check (H1 present, absolute links, opening paragraph) in each plugin repo's CI.

A real tester pass (about 5 people, as a pilot to find failures, not as a pass mark) on the two first-success journeys: install an app and run its example; create, initialise, release and download an installer. Time the real durations (CI wait, token set-up) and then put the measured numbers into the guides.

Plugin first-run section ('See a result in 5 minutes' with the existing screenshots F3/N5) in LabConstrictor-Tools docs/user-guide.md once the plugins leave 'Under heavy construction'; plus OPERATIONS.md troubleshooting facts surfaced in image-software.
Decide whether a missing sync token should make the weekly sync workflow skip rather than fail (template workflow change, maintainers' call).

reject.item: A mandatory standard template (audience chips, estimated time, tested version, Before/Instructions/Check/If it fails/Next) on every guide
reject.why: The benchmark itself limits it to task guides; imported guides have no metadata channel (title is the first H1, description the opening paragraph, links must be absolute); chips would be a new badge role needing DESIGN.md first. The three headings on five critical guides give most of the value.

reject.item: Tested-version stamps, 'Written for template version X' footers and 'Last checked: YYYY-MM' lines in guides
reject.why: Nothing written twice: the version already lives in the release tag, verified_version and template manifest; the template version is not a test statement, the docs are copied into all app repos, and a stale hand-typed date is worse than none. Use the existing per-app 'Verified for X on date' mechanism when a maintainer really verifies an app.

reject.item: PR previews for the plugin and guide repos via the site build, and a reusable site workflow for all repos
reject.why: scripts/fetch_guides.py --ref applies one ref to every repo it reads (including napari/napari, fiji/fiji, simple-icons), GitHub Pages has no per-PR URL, and the guides are 29-40 lines. A pre-merge contract check in each repo is the right-sized alternative (in 'later').

reject.item: Hard CI gate failing the build when a critical guide lacks a heading
reject.why: A heading rename in another repo would stop the daily Pages deploy while the issue opens in the site repo. Report first, fail later (item 9).

reject.item: Sample data and a scientific example required for every app or for listing an app, and redefining 'Verified' as 'maintainer ran the documented example'
reject.why: Author-controlled exposure and tiers: Community means automatic checks only; apps differ in kind (VLab4Mic simulates, no input data). The Verified definition is a policy decision for the user (see ask_user). A featured-app-without-quickstart build warning would fire daily on all three featured apps and open noise about repos the team does not own.

reject.item: A site-side 'First run' block, a 'Try an example' section and a new `examples` array in the manifest now
reject.why: Site already renders `quickstart` and `docs_url` (pages_apps.py:108-120); no app has used them yet. Duplicating the facts (format, dimensions, size) into the manifest writes them twice and risks silent drift. Revisit only if apps adopt the existing fields.

reject.item: Treat the LabConstrictor Demo app as the generic first-analysis tutorial
reject.why: Its only notebook (Image_Preview) is an upload-an-image preview with no sample image, no result, and its README is the template stub; calling it a tutorial would overstate it.

DESIGN.md 'Images' allows PNG, JPEG, GIF; the pictures live on the template doc_source branch and are copied as bytes. Prefer fewer GIFs, step screenshots and deep links; amend DESIGN.md first if video is ever wanted.

reject.item: Site-injected 'Check that it worked', 'If something fails' or 'Next' blocks, or a per-guide Next that overrides the generated pager, or a site-held synonym table in data/*.yaml replacing source edits
reject.why: Source of truth lives in each repo and the Edit-this-page link must point at the file containing the text. The pager already exists and must derive from the README order (Build) and data/guides.yaml (Use). The hidden-search-words file in item 7 is limited to about 10 justified synonyms, not a replacement for visible text.

reject.item: Uninstall, update and macOS/Linux steps and exact macOS dialog titles written from memory
reject.why: No source in the repos documents the macOS .pkg uninstall or update procedure, and Gatekeeper wording varies by macOS version. Write them only after a maintainer reproduces them on real machines.

reject.item: Moving the 115-line version cell out of notebook_upload.md into a new template file, and a 'Reference' manifest page now
reject.why: Adds a file that must stay in sync with the guide; low benefit versus the label fixes. Reference page is in 'later'.

reject.item: External-link checker in the deploy path and form-repo changes for the install-stub link (app.py:685) or a filename test
reject.why: AGENTS.md: build never goes online; the form line writes into the generated app README a relative link to that app's own download_executable.md, which is correct per app. The audit's premise was wrong.

reject.item: A GitHub Pages overrides/ no-results panel and a Playwright CI search test
reject.why: Depends on hashed theme internals and shadow DOM; fragile on theme updates and heavy for a small team. The help page and visible wording fix the zero-result cases instead.

reject.item: Analytics-based failure signals (visitor repeatedly opening troubleshooting pages), language selector, version selector, AI chatbot
reject.why: Site has no analytics and is unlisted; English-only is proportionate; benchmark's own 'do not build' list excludes the rest.

reject.item: Retitling the host guides' 'If something does not work' to 'My app does not show up in napari/Fiji/QuPath' and a hard tested-version stamp on plugin guides
reject.why: The section covers the failure dialog and log path, not only an unlisted app; discovery behaviour is unverified for each host; renaming also changes the anchor (redirects do not cover anchors).

ask_user.question: Should template synchronisation (fine-grained token, repository secret, about 15 GitHub actions) stay a mandatory step before the first initialisation, or move after the first release as an optional 'Keep your app up to date' guide?
ask_user.recommendation: Ask the template maintainers, then move it after the first release and replace the three gates with one recommendation sentence. A missing token only affects the weekly sync (sync_template.yml needs it only when a sync is required), but do not say the failure is harmless. If they want it early, keep the gate and add the one-sentence reason. Do the README reorder (item 8) either way.

ask_user.question: Do you want to redefine the 'Verified' tier (content/submit.md) as 'a maintainer ran the documented example', and should featured apps without a quickstart or docs_url get a build warning?
ask_user.recommendation: No, not yet. First get CellTracksColab and NucleiSky to publish a real example using the existing quickstart and docs_url fields (item 12). Revisit the Verified wording once one app has run its example, and keep any warning informational only after at least one app has a quickstart.

ask_user.question: Who can run clean installs on Windows, macOS and Linux and one throwaway initialise-to-release run on GitHub so labels, durations, expected outputs and macOS/Windows dialog wording can be confirmed before they are written down?
ask_user.recommendation: One maintainer, one afternoon, per OS and release; record OS, app release and date in the PR descriptions. This one run unlocks the held-back items in 5, 6 and 12: the macOS and 'browser stays empty' entries, the SmartScreen/unidentified-developer wording, install durations, the 'Check that it worked' texts, the NucleiSky and CellTracksColab example outputs. Until then, those lines stay unwritten, not guessed.

ask_user.question: Is the hard-coded canonical site address in the napari guide (cellmigrationlab.github.io/LabConstrictor-Site/...) the one to keep?
ask_user.recommendation: Confirm the canonical production URL and either use it everywhere or use a stable relative-free link; the fix belongs in napari-labconstrictor docs/user-guide.md (item 13).

acceptance_results: Persona runs (Playwright, Chromium, built site; the :8765 preview was down mid-run so a static server on site/ was used). Persona 3, someone seeing 'Windows protected your PC': PASS in 3 actions, about 5 s. Search for the exact dialog text returns /guides/install/#windows first, with the More info / Run anyway screenshot and alt text. Persona 1, finding an app: 2 clicks to the NucleiSky page, 'Your system' badge on the matching tile; but the journey STALLS after install. notebook-usage ends at 'Open the Notebook', nothing says what data to use, what the result looks like or where it is saved; NucleiSky ships no example images; 0 of 6 manifests use quickstart or docs_url. The 15-minute first-result target is unreachable today. Persona 2, building an app: 2 clicks to the first Build guide, but not completable without guessing. The template-synchronisation step is about 15 GitHub actions with no check or failure route; initialise has no numbered steps; the pager from executable-creation goes to the Colab authoring guide, not test/submit; template-synchronization prints its own footer as literal Markdown. A heading scan of 15 critical guides found check-style headings in 3, failure routes in 5, next-step headings in 2, time estimates in 1. Persona 4, Fiji user: reaches the Fiji guide in 3 clicks or by search ('Fiji'), but cannot finish: build-with-Maven or copy-a-script, no result shown, no ready file. Honest 'Under heavy construction' warnings mean nobody is misled. Search on the benchmark's nine queries: 5 of 9 reach an actionable page (Windows protected your PC, JupyterLab does not start, how to run a notebook, requirements.yaml, use inside Fiji); 4 fail with a blank panel or the wrong page: 'put my notebook online', 'GitHub build failed', 'app not showing in napari' return 0, 'Mac cannot open app' returns create-repository only. Zero hits in the index for damaged, unidentified, Gatekeeper, SmartScreen, ImageJ. Automated checks: scripts/check_site.py and check_design.py both report 38 pages, 0 problems; internal links, anchors, descriptions, h1 and alt presence are already guarded; the green result also proves the build does not detect guide completeness, literal Markdown in prose, or search outcomes. Human-only and not run here: 4-of-5 tester completion, the 15-minute first analysis, per-OS routes, screen-reader and keyboard checks; nothing was installed or run on a real OS and no measured durations exist. Skeptic notes: the claim that workflow-status Next loops to template-synchronization is false (it goes to troubleshooting); the guides' premise that download_executable.md should hold uninstall steps is only right per app repo, not for the template stub.
overlaps_with_app_centre_benchmark: Example data and a quickstart owned by the app repo: the manifest's existing quickstart (max 6 steps) and docs_url fields, which no listed app sets (item 12; later: a single optional `example` object).

Manifest field documentation and the template's app_manifest.md, including the 'quick start' line at line 31; the duplicated manifest example between content/submit.md and app_manifest.md (later: generate a Reference page from the schema).

Install deep links from the app page tiles to per-OS anchors in the install guide (item 3), and the install guide's 'Before you start' that points to the App Centre page for sizes and supported systems (item 5); the Intel-versus-Apple-Silicon facts are per-app (smoke_install.yml says Intel Macs are informational only), so the generic guide must not state them.
Trust and verification: the Verified tier definition in content/submit.md, the unused verified_version/verified_on mechanism (all 6 apps null), and the unsigned-installer notice in install.md.
Hub help blocks and the Submit step at the end of the Build path (data/hubs.yaml flow ends at /submit/); search-index noise from /apps/ card text (left alone for now).
Plugin and host integration: image-software and host guides' first-run line and 'ImageJ/Fiji' wording; the Intel/OS platform matrix shown on the app page.
